subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that skill's host run, while still blocking dangerous host override names and preserving cross-skill isolation?
rationale: The documented behavior and user reports support passing per-skill env into host exec, but the current block is a deliberate secret-handling boundary and the linked candidate PR overlaps prior inverse-leak fixes.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit env keys explicitly listed under that skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with focused tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and cross-skill isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only secret allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare every sensitive env name in metadata and update docs/doctor output so users do not expect arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys to work.

options.title: Move to a different secret contract
options.body: Defer the env bypass and instead design a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit env keys explicitly listed under that skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with focused tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and cross-skill isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the overlapping skill env, SecretRef, and regression-repair path.
